ascii-only.markdownDescription:
A line holds a character outside ASCII.

SystemVerilog tools differ in how they read other encodings; a stray non-breaking space or typographic quote breaks some of them and is invisible in review.

cast-as-task.markdownDescription:
`$cast` called as a task.

A failed task-form `$cast` is only a run-time error the simulator may continue past with the destination unchanged; call it as a function and report failure (LNG-20).

class-outside-package.markdownDescription:
A class declared outside a package.

Classes in packages have one definition the whole testbench shares; a class in a module or at compilation-unit scope is a separate type in each place (FIL-3).

compilation-unit-import.markdownDescription:
An `import` at compilation-unit scope.

An import outside a module, interface or package leaks into every file compiled after it, so a file's meaning depends on the compile order (FIL-4).

component-created-with-new.markdownDescription:
A component is created with `new` instead of the factory.

A component made with `new` cannot be overridden by a test (FAC-1); only TLM ports, exports, imps and analysis FIFOs are made with `new`.

constraint-name.markdownDescription:
A constraint is not named `<what>_cstr`.

One suffix makes constraints easy to find and to switch off by name (LNG-13).

coverage-weight-goal.markdownDescription:
`option.weight` or `option.goal` is set.

A goal under 100 hides holes, and weights turn the total into a negotiation (COV-7). Weight 0 on a coverpoint that only builds a cross is the exception.

create-name-chars.markdownDescription:
A factory `create` name has characters outside `[a-zA-Z0-9_]` or `__`.

Instance names appear in hierarchical paths, config-db lookups and logs; other characters break glob matching and tools (NAM-7).

create-name-matches.markdownDescription:
A factory `create` name differs from the variable it is assigned to.

Log paths then map directly to code (NAM-8).

default-sequence.markdownDescription:
`default_sequence` is set.

Default sequences start stimulus implicitly from configuration; start sequences explicitly from the test (SEQ-11).

delay-without-unit.markdownDescription:
A delay literal without a time unit.

A bare #10 means whatever the scope's time unit is; write #10ns (FIL-7).

direct-report-call.markdownDescription:
`uvm_report_info/warning/error/fatal` is called directly.

The report macros skip building the message when it is filtered; direct calls always build it (FAC-9).

display-in-uvm-class.markdownDescription:
`$display` in a class, or another reporting system task in a UVM class.

Classes must not use `$display`; UVM classes report only with the UVM report macros, which the test can filter, count and redirect (MSG-1).

end-comment.markdownDescription:
A comment follows `end` on its line.

End comments (`end // while (...)`) go stale when the code above changes; nothing checks them.

end-label.markdownDescription:
A class, function, task, module, interface, package, covergroup, property, sequence or clocking block ends without a label.

`endclass : bus_driver` is checked by the compiler; a comment is not.

extends-uvm-transaction.markdownDescription:
A class extends `uvm_transaction`.

Sequence items extend `uvm_sequence_item`, which sequences and sequencers expect (TRN-1).

extern-method.markdownDescription:
A class method declared `extern`.

Two copies of every signature cost more than they give; define methods in the class body (CLS-2).

factory-incompatible-constructor.markdownDescription:
The factory cannot call the constructor of a registered class.

The UVM factory constructs a component with new(name, parent) and an object with new() and new(name); a constructor that needs other arguments fails when the factory first creates the class, often far from the class itself.

field-macros-in-component.markdownDescription:
A `` `uvm_field_* `` macro in a component.

Field macros in a component trigger implicit config-db lookups (apply_config_settings); configuration is explicit in the style guide (FAC-4).

file-extension.markdownDescription:
A compiled file or an included file has the wrong extension.

Compiled units and files included into packages use .sv; .svh is for macro and header files only (FIL-2).

final-newline.markdownDescription:
The file does not end with exactly one newline.

A missing final newline joins the last line with whatever follows it (an `include, a concatenated file list); extra blank lines are noise.

formatter-drift.markdownDescription:
Lines differ from what the project's formatter makes.

A project that names its formatter keeps its code as the formatter makes it, so that layout is never argued about or changed by hand (FMT-13). Checked only when .dvicode/lint.json names DVICode's formatter ("formatter": "dvicode").

illegal-bins.markdownDescription:
`illegal_bins` in a covergroup.

Illegal values are errors that assertions or checkers must report; coverage only samples. Exclude values with `ignore_bins` (COV-6).

include-guard.markdownDescription:
An included file has no include guard named after it.

A guard makes a second `include harmless; naming it after the file (BUS_DRIVER_SV) avoids two files sharing one guard (FIL-6).

line-length.markdownDescription:
A line is longer than the limit.

Long lines are hard to read side by side in reviews and diffs.

max.description: the longest line allowed, in characters

tab-width.description: the columns a tab counts for

message-id-get-name.markdownDescription:
A report message ID is `get_name()`.

Instance names depend on where the class is instantiated and are already in the message header; IDs should be static and functional (MSG-2).

missing-super-phase-call.markdownDescription:
A function phase does not call `super.<phase>(phase)` first.

The parent's phase work (UVM's own, or a base class's) is skipped or runs late; CMP-4 asks for the call first in every function phase.

naming-case.markdownDescription:
A name is not in the case the style guide asks for.

lower_snake_case for classes, variables, functions, tasks, instances, signals, packages, interfaces and modules (as the UVM library); UPPER_SNAKE_CASE for parameters, localparams, enum literals and constant macros (NAM-1, NAM-2).

naming-prefix.markdownDescription:
A name starts with `uvm_` or `m_`.

`uvm_` belongs to the library and `m_` marks UVM internals; project names with them hide that distinction (NAM-3).

objection-without-description.markdownDescription:
`raise_objection`/`drop_objection` without a description.

The description is what `+UVM_OBJECTION_TRACE` shows (OBJ-4).

p-sequencer.markdownDescription:
`` `uvm_declare_p_sequencer ``.

It locks a sequence to one sequencer type (FAC-8); see SEQ-8 for alternatives.

pre-do-override.markdownDescription:
`pre_do`, `mid_do` or `post_do` is overridden.

These hooks run inside UVM's item flow and are easy to misuse; SEQ-14 allows them only to change a sequence that cannot be edited, together with a factory override.

program-block.markdownDescription:
A `program` block.

Program blocks change scheduling in ways that hide races instead of fixing them; the style guide does not use them (IFC-2).

randomize-in-assert.markdownDescription:
randomize() is called inside an assertion.

When assertions are turned off ($assertoff, a simulator option), the whole assertion is skipped, the randomize() call with it: the test silently runs on unrandomized values.

randomize-result-discarded.markdownDescription:
The result of randomize() is discarded.

randomize() returns 0 when the constraints cannot be met and then leaves the variables unchanged; a discarded result lets the test run on with stale values.

randomize-void-cast.markdownDescription:
The result of randomize() is discarded with void'(...).

The style guide asks for every randomize() result to be checked (LNG-10); `void'` only says the result is ignored on purpose.

suppression-not-waiver.markdownDescription:
A `dvicode-lint:` suppression.

Suppressions turn rules off for a region; the style guide's waiver record is a `// <ID> waived: <reason>` comment on the code it covers (§0).

suppression-unmatched.markdownDescription:
`dvicode-lint: enable=` without a `disable=` before it.

An enable that ends no suppression usually means the disable was removed or misspelled.

timescale.markdownDescription:
A `` `timescale `` directive.

`` `timescale `` leaks into every file compiled after it, so a file's time unit depends on compile order; declare `timeunit` and `timeprecision` in the package, module or interface instead (FIL-7).

timeunit-first.markdownDescription:
A scope with delays or time values does not declare timeunit and timeprecision first.

Without them the scope's time unit comes from compile order or tool defaults (FIL-7).

todo-format.markdownDescription:
A TODO is not written `TODO:<owner>:<P1|P2|P3>: <text>`.

A fixed form makes TODOs greppable and summarizable by owner and priority, and P1s can be checked before sign-off.

trailing-whitespace.markdownDescription:
A line ends in spaces or tabs.

Trailing whitespace is invisible noise in diffs and reviews.

uvm-class-not-registered.markdownDescription:
A concrete UVM class is not registered with the factory.

Only registered classes can be created and overridden through the factory (FAC-1, FAC-2); an unregistered class cannot be replaced from a test.

uvm-deprecated-api.markdownDescription:
Deprecated UVM API is used.

These parts of UVM were deprecated in UVM 1.2 and removed in IEEE 1800.2: code using them does not compile with a current UVM library (or with +define+UVM_NO_DEPRECATED).

uvm-do-macros.markdownDescription:
A `` `uvm_do ``, `` `uvm_create ``, `` `uvm_send `` or `` `uvm_rand_send `` macro.

These macros hide create, start_item, randomize and finish_item, and their randomization results; write the steps explicitly (FAC-7).

uvm-internal-member.markdownDescription:
A UVM internal member (`m_...`) is used.

Members whose names start with `m_` are UVM's internals: they change between UVM versions without notice (FAC-11). `m_sequencer` is documented and allowed.

uvm-override-signature.markdownDescription:
A UVM phase method is overridden with another signature.

A phase method only runs when it overrides UVM's own declaration exactly: a task where UVM declares a function, or other arguments, is either refused by the compiler late or never called.

uvm-registration-mismatch.markdownDescription:
A UVM registration macro does not fit its class.

The factory creates what the macro registers: another class's name, the object macro on a component, or a non-parameterized macro on a parameterized class registers the wrong thing or fails to compile only where the factory is used.

virtual-on-override.markdownDescription:
`virtual` is repeated on an override of a UVM virtual method.

An override of a virtual method is virtual anyway; the style guide keeps `virtual` for new methods that extensions may override (CLS-4).

waiver-unattached.markdownDescription:
A waiver is followed by no statement or declaration it could cover.

A waiver covers the statement or declaration right after it; one before `end`, `else` or the end of the file covers nothing.

waiver-unknown-id.markdownDescription:
A waiver or suppression names a rule that does not exist.

A misspelled rule ID waives nothing, so the finding it was meant for stays (or a later one goes unnoticed).

waiver-without-reason.markdownDescription:
A waiver or suppression gives no reason.

The style guide (§0) requires every waiver to say why the rule does not apply; a reason is what reviewers and later readers check.

rulesets.description: recommended: provable correctness rules; recommended-preview: correctness rules still under review; hexk: the HEXK SV/UVM Style Guide (includes the others)

baseline.description: A baseline file (written by `dvicode lint --write-baseline`), relative to the folder holding .dvicode: the findings it lists are not reported

extends.description: parent (default): start from the configuration above; none: from the defaults

formatter.description: The project's formatter (FMT-13): with "dvicode", the hexk rule formatter-drift reports lines DVICode's formatter would change

reason.description: Why these paths are linted differently
